name: Lifetime Software Deals Marketplace
demand: There is a demand proxy, but not a verified market-size estimate: AppSumo advertises over 2 million satisfied customers, a cumulative company claim rather than active users or category-wide demand: https://appsumo.com/?type=lifetime-deal. This listing claims 5,000+ purchasers in its body and metrics but 50K+ in its title; neither count is independently verified: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers. No verified search-volume, install, active-user, or repeat-purchase figures were found.
prices: The target's customer pricing and seller commission schedule are not public in the listing: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers. Current alternatives sell software deals at varied one-time prices: AppSumo shows examples at $49, $59 and $89, and its Plus membership is $99/year or $12/month: https://appsumo.com/?afsrc=1&irgwc=1 and https://appsumo.com/plus/. GrabLTD lists Pabbly Connect at $349 one-time and says it had 530+ live deals on 23 Oct 2026: https://grabltd.com/.

revenue_proof.claim: Acquire's public page claims $595,000 TTM revenue and $79,500 TTM profit and displays a P&L Documents label, but the underlying statements are not publicly accessible. The same page reports last-month profit as $7,100 in its metrics and $20,500 in its description. It gives no TTM period end or listing publication date, so the underlying event date and revenue remain unverified.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: unverified; TTM period end and listing date are not shown. The page was accessed 2026-10-23.

copy_speed: High for the storefront and marketplace mechanics. Day Zero presents a software lifetime-deal marketplace and was recorded as launched on 12 Oct 2026 by StackScope; its own site positions it as “AppSumo meets Kickstarter”: https://stackscope.dev/launch/sk4bzmld/day-zero and https://dayzero.ltd/. GrabLTD says it returned with a rebuilt marketplace on 14 Oct 2026 and lists 530+ deals: https://grabltd.com/. A turnkey AppSumo-style marketplace script was released on 1 Oct 2026 for $49: https://viserlab.com/product/visersumo-saas-launchpad-and-lifetime-deal-selling-marketplace/342. These show recent competition and low-cost replication of basic mechanics; they do not prove those entrants have meaningful sales.
platform_risk: The listing says the business runs on Shopify and names AppSumo as a competitor, not as its platform provider: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers. Shopify permits store ownership transfers, but its transfer guidance calls for handling domains, payout details, third-party payment accounts and contracts, and says some business arrangements may need Shopify Support: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/your-account/manage-orgs-and-stores/change-transfer-ownership. Supply continuity is also a risk: AppSumo says it does not build or control partner products and cannot control if they pivot or shut down: https://help.appsumo.com/article/34-what-is-a-lifetime-deal. The target's traffic sources, vendor contracts and seller concentration are not disclosed.
defensible_asset: The only qualifying moat candidate is a two-sided network effect: the listing claims a business founded in January 2018, 150 SKUs and 5,000+ purchasers. But its title says 50K+, and it supplies no active-buyer count, active-seller count, repeat-purchase rate, exclusivity or marketplace liquidity data: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers. The public evidence does not establish proprietary compiled data, a maintained rules engine or meaningful switching costs. Current aggregators and marketplaces offer many alternatives: https://grabltd.com/ and https://appsumo.com/?type=lifetime-deal. Treat the network moat as possible but unproven.
build_effort: A basic Shopify-style catalog and checkout look straightforward to reproduce; the $49 marketplace script released 1 Oct 2026 is evidence that core mechanics are commoditized: https://viserlab.com/product/visersumo-saas-launchpad-and-lifetime-deal-selling-marketplace/342. Building the vendor supply, buyer trust, useful curation and repeat purchasing would be the hard part. For an AI-agent-run operator, order administration, listing drafts, routine support triage and reporting look automatable, while deal selection, vendor terms, exceptions and disputes still require human oversight. The listing provides no task breakdown or staffing roles, only a “small” team of 2–20: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers.
channel: Use SEO and comparison pages, inbound seller submissions, marketplace or affiliate partnerships, and integrations; send deal alerts only to people who opt in. Do not use cold email, SMS, DMs or calls. UK ICO guidance says electronic mail includes email, text and social direct messages, and rules differ for corporate subscribers versus sole traders and individuals; check recipient-country rules as well: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/.
owner_hours_per_week: unverified; the listing gives no seller-hours figure or post-sale staffing/retention plan. It reports a small team of 2–20, which does not establish that Ricardo could stay within 5 hours/week: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers.
automation_reason: Truly unknowable from the public evidence: there is no workflow or time-by-task breakdown, and the listing only describes a small team and a Shopify stack. Agents could plausibly handle routine order administration, support triage, content drafts and reporting, but vendor curation, negotiations and exception handling may be substantial. The available evidence cannot establish that agents would perform at least 50% of all work: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers.
listing_check: Not acquisition-cleared. Revenue: seller-stated $595K TTM revenue/$79.5K TTM profit only; the P&L file is not publicly viewable. Acquire says it does not conduct in-depth seller due diligence, and the listing's “Verified business” badge means US address and incorporation certificate verified, not financials: https://help.acquire.com/seller-faqs-1 and https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers. Churn/retention: subscription churn is not the relevant measure for one-off purchases, but repeat-buyer cohorts, seller attrition, refunds and chargebacks are unverified; the listing defines customers as unique purchasers and gives no retention data: same Acquire URL. Owner hours: unverified. Price/profit: the displayed $150K ask divided by claimed $79.5K TTM profit is 1.89x, but the same listing's price reasoning says $416.5K at 5.2x; last-month profit also conflicts ($7.1K versus $20.5K): same Acquire URL. Transferability: Shopify has a transfer process, but the target's domain, payment accounts, staff, seller contracts, IP and vendor permissions are not verified as transferable: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/your-account/manage-orgs-and-stores/change-transfer-ownership. Customer-data transfer also needs acquisition due diligence on purpose, lawful basis, transparency and governance: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/data-sharing/data-sharing-a-code-of-practice/due-diligence/. Seller dependence and a <=5-hour owner workload remain unverified.
moat_assessment: It survived the cheap kill-check because a marketplace network effect is plausible, but the public listing does not prove an active or durable network. The conflicting 5,000+/50K+ buyer count, lack of seller and repeat-purchase metrics, current competing marketplaces and the $49 clone script leave the moat weak until diligence verifies buyer liquidity, seller retention and transferable seller relationships: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers, https://grabltd.com/, and https://viserlab.com/product/visersumo-saas-launchpad-and-lifetime-deal-selling-marketplace/342.
desk_test: Cheapest useful one-workday screen: ask for private listing access through Acquire, then reconcile dated monthly P&L figures against Shopify orders/refunds and payment-processor payouts; check repeat purchases/refunds; inspect the vendor terms and redemption rights for the highest-revenue deals; and get a written owner-hours/task breakdown. Pass only if the seller explains the ask/profit and monthly-profit conflicts, proves the earnings, demonstrates transferable supply and shows a credible <=5-hour owner workload. Acquire says private listing information requires Premium or Platinum access and seller approval; current plan cost is not verified, so do not pay for access until the seller confirms they will provide these records: https://help.acquire.com/how-to-sign-up-on-acquire.com and https://help.acquire.com/seller-faqs-1.
red_flags: Do not acquire on the current public evidence. The price rationale conflicts with the ask; monthly profit differs between two parts of the listing; the title's 50K+ customer claim conflicts with the 5,000+ body/metric; revenue date and financial verification are absent; annual growth is listed as 0%; repeat buying, refunds, seller churn, owner hours, staff roles and vendor-contract transferability are not shown. The listing gives seller reasons as lack of time and starting a new venture, and reports a 2–20-person team, but provides no post-sale staffing plan: https://app.acquire.com/public/g7g5j7hjhs-profitable-lifetime-software-deals-marketplace-595k-ttm-revenue-50k-customers. Lifetime deal fulfillment depends on independent software vendors whose products may shut down: https://help.appsumo.com/article/34-what-is-a-lifetime-deal.
